examples.trans: She feels very lonely and sad right now.

examples.text: Вообще-то мы хотели спокойно посидеть девочками.
examples.trans: Actually we wanted to sit quietly with the girls.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'elevator' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Он целовался тут у лифта!
examples.trans: He was kissing right here by the elevator!

examples.text: А кто тогда целовался около лифта с сотрудницей?
examples.trans: Then who was kissing a female employee near the elevator?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Любимый мужчина готовит мне вкусный ужин.
examples.trans: My beloved man is cooking me a delicious dinner.

examples.text: Смотри, твой су-шеф сейчас звонит.
examples.trans: Look, your sous-chef is calling right now.

examples.text: Поставь телефон на громкую связь.
examples.trans: Put the phone on speakerphone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'отрудница'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common feminine noun meaning 'female employee' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А кто тогда целовался около лифта с сотрудницей?
examples.trans: Then who was kissing a female employee near the elevator?

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть сотрудница.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always female employee.

meanings.en: to calm down, to settle down
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спокоиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'calm down', paired with 'успокаиваться'.

examples.text: Ну что, успокоился?
examples.trans: Well, have you calmed down?

examples.text: Успокойся, пожалуйста!
examples.trans: Calm down, please!

examples.text: Успокойся, всё хорошо.
examples.trans: Calm down, everything's fine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Лена, у меня всё в порядке!
examples.trans: Lena, everything is fine with me!

examples.text: Я потом тебе всё подробно расскажу.
examples.trans: I will tell you everything in detail later.

examples.text: Пусть они лучше сами во всём разбираются.
examples.trans: Let them figure everything out by themselves.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'сказать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will tell', paired with 'рассказывать'.

examples.text: Расскажи, что случилось.
examples.trans: Tell me what happened.

examples.text: Я всё расскажу маме.
examples.trans: I'll tell Mum everything.

examples.text: Сталину расскажите.
examples.trans: Tell that to Stalin.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'am waiting for', paired with 'подождать'.

examples.text: Вообще непонятно, чего от него ждать.
examples.trans: There is no telling what to expect from him.

examples.text: Шеф, вы бы меня хоть предупреждали!
examples.trans: Chef, you could at least warn me!

examples.text: Не жди меня.
examples.trans: Don't wait for me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Любимый мужчина готовит мне вкусный ужин.
examples.trans: My beloved man is cooking me a delicious dinner.

examples.text: Смотри, твой су-шеф сейчас звонит.
examples.trans: Look, your sous-chef is calling right now.

examples.text: Завтра можете вообще на работу не приходить.
examples.trans: Tomorrow you do not have to come to work at all.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('honest').

examples.text: Знаешь, если честно, мне они тоже надоели.
examples.trans: You know, to be honest, I was tired of it too.

examples.text: Скажи честно, ты там в кабинете один?
examples.trans: Tell me honestly, are you alone in the office?

examples.text: Я жду от тебя честного ответа!
examples.trans: I am waiting for an honest answer from you!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'answer' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Хорошо, я только эту тележку отвезу.
examples.trans: Alright, I will just wheel this cart away.

examples.text: Я жду от тебя честного ответа!
examples.trans: I am waiting for an honest answer from you!

examples.text: Спасибо за честный ответ.
examples.trans: Thank you for the honest answer.
